title: Thread Weave: customer compact brief and request synthesis (May 2026)
content:
Executive snapshot:

This is a compact synthesis ("Thread Weave") of recent field conversations with five mid-market and two enterprise customers (pods A–E). Goal: surface the highest-confidence asks + quick probes we can run with engineering and solutions to (1) unblock short-term adoption friction, (2) validate where product work yields largest MRR/retention lift, and (3) capture easy ops patches for CS enablement.

Topline themes (high-level):
- Predictable unit cost & billing visibility: heavy signal across customers that token-attribution for mixed workloads (chat + embeddings + reranking) is opaque and causes finance friction.
- Failure-mode tolerance & graceful fallback: customers with hybrid Dedicated + Hosted strategies need transparent fallback rules and clear SLA trade-offs when Dedicated is at capacity.
- Fine-grained observability: requests want token-level traces correlated to routes, model versions, and customer request IDs — not just aggregate per-route stats.
- Private deployment friction: KMS rotation, auditability (HSM logs), and deterministic startup times for on-prem/air-gapped installs.
- Embeddings scale/UX: bulk upsert semantics, conflict resolution, and more explicit cost heuristics for large batch indexing.

Representative customer quotes (verbatim fragments):
- "We saw a 30% cost delta between our dev and prod traffic but couldn't explain why — the console charts are fuzzy." (Pod C - fintech)
- "When dedicated falls over, we want a policy that says 'serve degraded but local-first' rather than opaque timeouts." (Pod A - consumer search)
- "We need to rotate keys offline and provide a signed attestation for auditors; vendor-managed rotation doesn't cut it." (Pod E - healthcare)

Priority lanes (hypothesis + quick metric to validate):
1) Billing transparency lane
   - Hypothesis: Adding per-route per-model token attribution and a cost-explain report will reduce billing disputes by 60% for customers surveyed.
   - Validation metric: #support-billing tickets per customer month (baseline) and time-to-resolve.
   - Low-effort probe: Add a downloadable CSV in Console with token breakdown for last 7 days (route, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_cost).

2) Graceful fallback / capacity policy lane
   - Hypothesis: Explicit fallback policies in the deployment config (serve-variant: degrade | queue | error) will reduce client-incurred downtime and improve perceived reliability.
   - Validation metric: number of failed requests vs successful fallbacks during simulated capacity loss in Dedicated test cluster.
   - Probe: Ship a canary UI in Console (experimental) to define per-route fallback policies and expose current active policy in traces.

3) Observability and trace correlation lane
   - Hypothesis: Token-level tracing for top 5 routes will decrease time-to-debug by 40% for SREs and solutions engineers.
   - Validation metric: mean time to root cause (MTTR) on recent incidents involving incorrect prompts or KV cache misses.
   - Probe: Pilot token-level trace export (compressed) for two customers — instrument SDK to attach request_id and client_trace_id.

Concrete feature asks (compiled and normalized):
- Cost explain export (console): downloadable CSV + per-request attribution (route, model, temp, tokens). Owner: Product-hosted-api.
- Fallback policy flags (api + console): per-route policy, canary rollout, auto-failover order. Owner: Product-console + Serving-runtime.
- Token-level trace correlation: request_id propagation, token timing, KV cache hit/miss markers. Owner: Observability + Serving-runtime.
- Dedicated burst autoscaling guardrails: short-term burst capacity with guaranteed best-effort vs reserved. Owner: Dedicated product + Infra.
- Private deployment KMS key rotation workflow (offline support + rotation report PDF). Owner: Private-deployments + Security.
- Embeddings bulk-upsert API and conflict resolution strategies (upsert-only, merge-policy, dedupe-by-hash). Owner: Hosted-api + Optimize.

Impact vs Effort quick mapping (subjective):
- High impact / low effort: cost explain CSV export; fallback policy UI toggles; improved support doc templates for billing.
- High impact / medium effort: token-level traces (pilot); embeddings bulk-upsert.
- Medium impact / high effort: Private KMS offline attestation flow; Dedicated burst autoscaling policy engine.

Unresolved signals and open questions to triage (for Eng/Product):
- Which existing tracing data points are safe to surface without PII leakage for customers on Shared-hosted? (security/privacy gating).
- What is the cost/throughput penalty for enabling token-level traces on production serving runtime across p99 latency SLAs?
- How to map token attribution to mixed-model pipelines where a single user request fans out to multiple model calls?

Suggested immediate next steps (30 / 60 day):
- 7 days: CS to run a focused poll across top-20 paying customers to confirm priority of Billing vs Observability asks; synthesize results into Confluence page. Owner: Priya.
- 14 days: Engineering to scope a minimal CSV export implementation (APIs and Console link) and estimate dev days. Owner: Evan + Eng infra lead.
- 30 days: Launch billing CSV pilot with Pods B/C and collect support ticket delta. Owner: CS + Product-hosted-api.
- 60 days: If pilot shows >25% reduction in query tickets/time-to-resolve, prioritize richer per-request explain in the roadmap.

Patchwork / quick CS playbook (scripts & templates):
- Support template: "How to explain token billing" (one-pager with examples for chat + embeddings mixed flows).
- Troubleshooting checklist: Dedicated fallback — how to validate fallback policy is active, reading Console liveness.
- Pre-sales FAQ: private deployment audits — list of current attestations and gaps.

Notes to self (scratch):
- Mentioned Slack threads: #cs-billing, #dedicated-failovers — link later in Confluence.
- Possible cross-team sync: Product + Serving-runtime + Observability next Wed. Suggest 30m cross-functional stand.

Appendix: quick raw signal snippets (unedited):
- "We're losing faith in the numbers — the token counts jump when we switch to long-context prompts." (Pod B)
- "A fallback that serves a smaller model automatically with a human-readable reason would be ideal." (Pod D)

End of brief.
